title: Start likely-needed work early only when it is reversible and cannot change accepted behavior

facts.note: Task, plan or doc text mentions starting likely-needed work before it is confirmed.

values: work is started before its need is confirmed (proposed in a plan/wagon/WMBT/acceptance/doc or already implemented)
facts.note: Whether a step is speculative, and whether it touches authority commits, irreversible or externally visible effects or data access, can only be judged by reading the plan or change. Applies regardless of how expensive the work is or which phase introduces it.
Detecting implemented speculative work in a diff needs a new diff-level observer.

fires: A plan proposes precomputing or prefetching results before the upstream step confirms they are needed.
A wagon or WMBT plans to start a likely next journey step in parallel and discard it if the prediction is wrong.
Speculative work (cheap or expensive) is introduced or found during implementation and must be planned or reviewed for reversibility.
A cheap early-start step would perform an externally visible mutation or authority commit.
doesNotFire: A plan that executes steps only after their trigger is confirmed (no early or predicted work).
Plans that only reference existing, declared runtime dispatch options without introducing early/predicted work.

given: Work that may be needed later is proposed or implemented to start before its need is confirmed (any cost, any phase)
when: the planner authors or reviews that step in a plan, wagon, WMBT, acceptance or doc
then: Allow the speculative work only if it is reversible and discarding or cancelling it cannot change accepted behavior.
prefer: Consider when expensive future work is predictable and wasted work can be budgeted.
Define isolation, cancellation and resource budgets for the speculative work.
Test wrong predictions, cancellation races, duplicate attempts, isolation and total wasted work; measure net benefit.
avoid: Speculating authority commits, irreversible side effects, externally visible mutations or unauthorized data access.
Assuming a generic speculative journey scheduler exists or using this pattern to authorize undeclared execution.
Inferring unimplemented orchestration behavior or a new runtime dispatch option from this pattern.
why: Speculation saves latency only if wrong guesses are harmless; work that commits authority, mutates visibly or is irreversible cannot be cleanly discarded and would change accepted behavior.
evidence: Isolation, cancellation and resource budgets are defined for each speculative step.
Wrong predictions, cancellation races, duplicate attempts, isolation and total wasted work are tested, and net benefit is measured.
No speculative step performs an authority commit, irreversible side effect, externally visible mutation or unauthorized data access.
Existing plan and source validators pass; the work relies only on declared runtime execution, not an assumed speculative scheduler.
verifier_detail: Guidance for agents, not independent enforcement; no dedicated detector. Compliance is reviewed via existing plan and source validators plus review of the plan/change.
audit: Source term ids: applicability, constraints, evidence, runtime_boundary
Graph: requires planner.journey.execution-strategies (shared applicability and evidence principles).
